stemBlocks.value: Write the number 58.736 correct to: (i) the nearest whole number  (ii) three significant figures  (iii) two decimal places.
Think first: Each part asks you to cut the number at a different place, so identify the cut position before you look at any digit.

solutionSteps.instruction: Round to the nearest whole number.

contentBlocks.value: Keep 58; the next digit is 7, which is 5 or more, so round up
The first three significant figures are 5, 8 and 7; the next digit is 3, which is less than 5
Keep 58.73; the next digit is 6, which is 5 or more, so round the 3 up

strategyBlocks.value: For each part, find the last digit you are keeping, look at the digit immediately after it, and round up if that digit is 5 or more.

whyThisWorks.value: Rounding replaces a number by the nearest one available at the chosen level of precision, and the digit immediately after the cut decides which side is nearer. Significant figures count from the first non-zero digit, so they measure precision relative to the size of the number, while decimal places count from the point and measure absolute precision. That is why the same number gives three different answers here.

commonErrors.misconception: Rounding 58.736 in stages — 58.74 to 58.7 to 59 — instead of judging each part from the original number.

examTip.value: Always round from the original number, never from an answer you have already rounded — chained rounding is the most common way a correct method loses its mark.
